title: Prime-to-residue-characteristic uniformizer root extensions
statement: Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $F$, algebraically closed residue field $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$, and uniformizer $\pi$. For every positive integer $m$ prime to $p$, all roots in a separable closure of $F$ [def-pd-separable-closure] of $X^m-1$ belong to $R$. If $\alpha^m=\pi$ in that separable closure, then the splitting field $L$ of $X^m-\pi$ is $F(\alpha)$, is cyclic Galois of degree $m$ over $F$, and has ramification index $m$ at the unique maximal ideal of the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Tag 0BUB (lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure), final proof paragraph: splitting field of X^m minus a uniformizer and divisibility of its ramification index; for the stated henselian specialization and equality, algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian, simple-root lifting) and the degree bound [F(alpha):F] <= m; more-algebra.tex Tag 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension), the degree/ramification formula giving e <= [L:F].

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$ prime to $p$. Its image in the residue field is nonzero, hence $m$ is a unit in $R$. Since the residue field is algebraically closed, it is separably closed and $R$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. By [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity], the group of $m$th roots of unity in $R$ has cardinality $m$. Mathlib's HasEnoughRootsOfUnity gives a primitive root $\zeta$. Its images in $F$ and $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$ remain primitive by injectivity. Every $m$th root in $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is a power of this image, so lies in the image of $R$.

source.place: Tags 04GF and 04GG, simple-root lifting; realized by the existing strict-local roots-of-unity lemma.

proof.text: For a chosen root $\alpha$, put $L=F(\alpha)$ and $a=\alpha\in L$. Let $f=X^m-\pi$, $A=R[T]/(f)$ and let $t$ be the class of $T$. The uniformizer $\pi$ is irreducible [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. By [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra], $A$ is a DVR domain with maximal ideal $(t)$. Monicity gives that $A$ is finite over $R$, using the finite-module clause of [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. Evaluation $t\mapsto a$ defines $j:A\to L$. It is injective: every nonzero element of a DVR is $ut^r$ with $u$ a unit, and its image is nonzero since $a^m=\pi\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 09EV (lemma-pull-root-uniformizer), proof for the standard root algebra; includes m=1 via the cited existing node.

proof.text: The polynomial $f=X^m-\pi$ is Eisenstein at the prime maximal ideal $(\pi)$: its leading coefficient is one, all lower coefficients belong to $(\pi)$, and its constant coefficient $-\pi$ does not belong to $(\pi)^2$. Indeed $\pi=\pi^2b$ would cancel to $1=\pi b$, contradicting that $\pi$ is a nonunit. Apply [lem-per-eisenstein-prime-ideal-criterion], packaged as Polynomial.IsEisensteinAt.irreducible, using primitivity of a monic polynomial. Mathlib's monic Gauss lemma (Polynomial.Monic.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_fraction_map) transfers irreducibility to $F[X]$. This replaces the planned coefficient-clearing argument.

Construct $L=F(\alpha)$ explicitly. The identity $a^m=\pi$ and the primitive $m$th root from Step 1 show that $X^m-\pi$ splits over $L$, by Mathlib's X_pow_sub_C_splits_of_isPrimitiveRoot. The integral generator $a$ is a root and generates $L$ as an $F$-algebra, so $L$ is a splitting field. Apply [lem-exc-kummer-binomial-splitting-field] with irreducibility from Step 3. It gives that $L/F$ is Galois, its Galois group is cyclic, and its degree is $m$.

source.place: Tag 09I6 (section-Kummer), opening paragraph; exact field-theoretic conclusions supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Extend the injection $j:A\to L$ to a map $g:\operatorname{Frac}(A)\to L$. Its field range contains $F$, since every element of $F$ is a ratio of elements of $R$, and contains $a=g(t)$. Since $L=F(a)$, $g$ is surjective and hence identifies $L$ as a fraction field of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], the DVR $A$ is integrally closed in $L$. Since $A$ is integral over $R$, it is an integral closure of $R$ in $L$: every element integral over $R$ is integral over $A$ and hence lies in $A$, and all elements of $A$ are integral over $R$. The uniqueness equivalence IsIntegralClosure.equiv identifies $A$ with the concrete integralClosure $R$ $L$ of [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Transport the DVR structure across this equivalence. Its unique maximal ideal is generated by the image of $t$.

source.place: Tag 09EV, proof identifying the normal standard root algebra with the integral closure.

proof.text: Let $B$ be the integral closure and $q$ its maximal ideal generated by the image $b$ of $t$. Transporting $t^m=\pi$ gives $b^m=\pi$, so the extended maximal ideal of $R$ is $q^m$. Integrality shows that $q$ contracts to the maximal ideal of $R$. The ideal $q$ is nonzero because its irreducible generator $b$ is nonzero. In the Dedekind domain $B$, powers of the nonzero proper ideal $q$ are strictly decreasing, so the extended ideal is contained in $q^m$ but not $q^{m+1}$. Ideal.ramificationIdx'_spec and Ideal.ramificationIdx'_eq_ramificationIdx' identify its ramification index as $m$. This works for $m=1$ as well, with trivial cyclic group and degree and ramification index one.

source.place: Tag 09E4 (definition-extension-discrete-valuation-rings), definition of ramification index; Tag 09EV (4).

lean.statement: theorem tame_root_extension (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [HenselianLocalRing R] (F : Type v) [Field F] [Algebra R F] [IsFractionRing R F] (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) [IsAlgClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)] [CharP (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) p] (π : R) (hπ : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R = Ideal.span {π}) (Fsep : Type w) [Field Fsep] [Algebra F Fsep] [Algebra R Fsep] [IsScalarTower R F Fsep] [IsSepClosure F Fsep] (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hmp : ¬p ∣ m) : (∀ ζ : Fsep, ζ ^ m = 1 → ∃ r : R, algebraMap R Fsep r = ζ) ∧ ∀ α : Fsep, α ^ m = algebraMap R Fsep π → ∃ L : IntermediateField F Fsep, IsSplittingField F L (X ^ m - C (algebraMap R F π)) ∧ L = IntermediateField.adjoin F {α} ∧ IsGalois F L ∧ IsCyclic (Gal(L / F)) ∧ Module.finrank F L = m ∧ ∃ q : Ideal (integralClosure R L), q.IsMaximal ∧ (∀ q' : Ideal (integralClosure R L), q'.IsMaximal → q' = q) ∧ q.ramificationIdx R = m
